search_objective: Identify authoritative sources reporting West Nile virus cases, deaths, hospitalizations, and surveillance data for California during August 2024 (2024-08-01 to 2024-08-31), covering all target fields: confirmed/probable/suspected/unspecified cases, deaths, hospitalizations, subnational and local locations, and date reported.
search_reasoning: The upstream planned queries are a reasonable starting point but have several weaknesses that reduce their effectiveness in iteration 1: (1) They use overly rigid exact-phrase matching (e.g., "WNV California August 2024") that is unlikely to match real agency page titles or report language; (2) They embed the date range string "2024-08-01-2024-08-31" literally in queries, which will not match natural-language reporting; (3) They do not target the specific California state and county public health agencies that are the primary authoritative sources for WNV in California — namely CDPH (California Department of Public Health) and county vector control/health departments; (4) They do not target the CDC ArboNET surveillance system, which is the national structured database for WNV; (5) The literature queries are low-value for a 2024 August window since peer-reviewed publications on a single month's data would not yet exist. For iteration 1 (max 4 queries), priority should be: (a) CDPH official WNV surveillance page for 2024, (b) CDC WNV surveillance/ArboNET for California 2024, (c) county-level California public health WNV reports for August 2024, and (d) news coverage of WNV in California in August 2024 to surface any outbreak alerts or press releases. Queries should use natural search language targeting agency names and report types, not rigid exact-phrase date strings.

query_batch.query: California Department of Public Health West Nile virus 2024 cases deaths surveillance report
query_batch.query_rationale: CDPH is the primary authoritative source for statewide WNV surveillance in California. Their annual or weekly WNV activity reports will contain confirmed/probable case counts, deaths, hospitalizations, and county-level breakdowns for 2024, including the August window. Using agency name + disease + year in natural language is more likely to surface the correct landing page than rigid exact-phrase matching.
query_batch.expected_source_type_or_evidence: CDPH West Nile virus surveillance page, annual summary, or weekly activity report for 2024
query_batch.expected_trust_signal: cdph.ca.gov domain; official state agency authorship; tabular case counts by county and week

query_batch.query: CDC West Nile virus 2024 California cases ArboNET surveillance statistics
query_batch.query_rationale: CDC's ArboNET system is the national arboviral surveillance database and publishes state-level WNV case counts including California. The CDC WNV activity page is updated regularly during transmission season and will contain confirmed neuroinvasive and non-neuroinvasive case counts, deaths, and state breakdowns for 2024. This is a critical cross-validation source against CDPH data.
query_batch.expected_source_type_or_evidence: CDC WNV activity and surveillance data page or ArboNET state-level table for 2024
query_batch.expected_trust_signal: cdc.gov domain; ArboNET attribution; tabular state-by-state case counts

query_batch.query: West Nile virus California county August 2024 cases deaths public health department report
query_batch.query_rationale: California WNV activity is heavily concentrated in specific counties (Los Angeles, Sacramento, Kern, Fresno, Riverside, San Bernardino). County-level health departments and vector control districts publish their own WNV activity reports and press releases, which may contain locality-level case counts and dates not aggregated in state-level reports. This query targets county-level official sources for August 2024 specifically.
query_batch.expected_source_type_or_evidence: County public health department press releases, vector control district activity reports, or local health officer advisories for August 2024
query_batch.expected_trust_signal: County .gov or .ca.gov domains; vector control district authorship; dated press releases or activity bulletins

query_batch.query: West Nile virus California August 2024 outbreak cases deaths news
query_batch.query_rationale: News coverage of WNV in California during August 2024 can surface outbreak alerts, public health press releases cited in media, and county-specific case counts that may not yet appear in structured surveillance databases. News articles often quote official figures and link to primary agency sources, providing both evidence quotes and pointers to authoritative URLs. August is peak WNV transmission season in California, making news coverage likely.
query_batch.expected_source_type_or_evidence: News articles from California regional outlets, wire services, or public health beat reporters citing official WNV case counts for August 2024
query_batch.expected_trust_signal: Dateline August 2024; direct citation of CDPH, county health department, or vector control district figures; named official spokesperson quotes

language_or_localization_reasoning: All queries are in English. California public health reporting is conducted exclusively in English at the state and county agency level. WNV surveillance reports from CDPH, CDC, and county health departments are published in English. No localization to other languages is needed for this jurisdiction and disease combination. The disease is referred to as "West Nile virus" (full name) and "WNV" (abbreviation) in official U.S. public health reporting — both terms are used across the query batch to maximize recall.
trust_considerations: Prefer sources with explicit .gov or .ca.gov domains for case count data
CDPH and CDC are tier-1 authoritative sources; county health departments are tier-2
News articles are acceptable as collection support only if they cite a named official source or agency report with specific numeric figures
Avoid sources that aggregate or repackage data without citing primary agency — these should not be used as primary evidence
CDC ArboNET data may lag real-time by several weeks; CDPH weekly reports are more timely for the August 2024 window

WNV case classification in California follows CDC ArboNET case definitions: neuroinvasive disease (confirmed) vs. non-neuroinvasive (confirmed) vs. probable — queries should surface sources that distinguish these categories

If these are not found, iteration 2 should target county health departments (e.g., Los Angeles, Sacramento, Kern, Fresno) and ProMED/news sources directly.
